newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela CVG toxic waste removal to cost $175 mln.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela CVG toxic waste removal to cost $175 mln.

text.p: Purchasers of state-owned metal companies in Venezuela will have to spend $174.8 million over five years to eliminate toxic wastes accumulated by the plants, a top government official said.
"We do not have the financing to confront this problem," said Elias Ynaty, president of state holding Corporacion Venezolana de Guayana (CVG).

According to figures presented to Congress by Ynaty, Venezuela's four-company aluminum sector requires investments of $109.8 million over five years to dispose of accumulated toxic wastes and reduce toxic emissions.
Steel company Sidor requires a similar investment of $64 million and ferro-silica company Fesilven $1 million, the document said.
The Venezuelan government plans to sell a controlling interest in its aluminum sector on Jan 31. Sidor and Fesilven are to be sold later in the first quarter of 1997.
